newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan bourse, driven by blue chips, closes up.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan bourse, driven by blue chips, closes up.

text.p: The Casablanca stock market closed on Monday 0.72 percent higher with activity focusing on leading stocks trading in small volumes, a stockbroker said.
The all-share index closed at 521.27 points from 517.54 points on Friday.
"The market is still illiquid with the same stocks driving it," a broker at Casablanca-based ABN Amro Finance said.
ONA group, the first biggest private holding, added five dirhams to close at 645 dirhams.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, Morocco's second largest conglomerate which holds diversified stakes in more than 40 firms, was up one dirham to 597 dirhams.
The conglomerate has a market capitalisation of more than 5.6 billion dirhams.
Banque Marocaine pour le Commerce et l'Industrie gained 11 dirhams to 404 dirhams.
Leading stock Wafabank remained unchanged at 675 dirhams.
Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, a blue chip stock, fell five dirhams to trade at 470 dirhams.
"The stock is volatile but it can still reach 500 dirhams," he added.
Samir oil refinery, the country's main refinery, soared eight dirhams to close at 287 dirhams.
Morocco floated 30 percent of the refinery in March 1996 which raised a total of 2.66 billion dirhams ($290 million). It plans to offer for sale 35 percent to 51 percent.
Steel mill Sonasid took 20 dirhams to close at 410 dirhams.

Morocco launched an international tender last week for sale of between 35 and 62 percent of Sonasid. It offered 35 percent of the state-owned giant last year in a flotation worth 420 million dirhams. It was oversubscribed with demand totalling 675 million dirhams.
Newly-floated Credor advanced by 18 dirhams to 641 dirhams.
"There are forecasts of better than expected annual results but the stock is still overvalued," he said.
Traded volume on the official market was 51.4 million from 99.9 million dirhams the previous session.
